llm.reply:
The knowledge graph links three genes to Li-Fraumeni syndrome [2]. The first is NCBIGene:7157, tumor protein p53 [4]. The second is NCBIGene:11200, checkpoint kinase 2 [3]. The third is NCBIGene:1029, cyclin dependent kinase inhibitor 2A [1].

## TP53 as primary cause

The literature presents germline TP53 mutation as the defining cause [19: "a cancer predisposition syndrome caused by a germline mutation of the TP53 gene on chromosome 17p13.1"]. The syndrome is inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern [19: "autosomal dominant pattern of inheritance with high penetrance"]. Mutations cause loss of p53 function, which permits tumour development [19: "TP53 gene mutations cause the loss of function of p53, leading to downstream events permissive for development of various malignancies"]. One case report found a deleterious germline missense change in exon 5 [21: "the germinal mutation c.527G>T (p.Cys176Phe) on exon 5 of the TP53 gene"].

## Sources of phenotypic heterogeneity

Clinical presentation varies even among carriers of the same variant [22: "Phenotypic heterogeneity is present among different families affected by the same pathogenic variant in TP53 gene"]. Proposed modifiers include variants in related genes and copy number changes [22: "polymorphic variants in TP53 gene or in TP53-related genes, copy number variations in particular regions"].

## Clinical research

Registered studies include whole-body MRI surveillance in p53 mutation carriers [20]. Another study examines the role of p53 in metabolism in affected patients [11].

The knowledge graph links four gene records to Li-Fraumeni syndrome. NCBIGene:1029 is cyclin dependent kinase inhibitor 2A [1]. NCBIGene:11200 is checkpoint kinase 2 [3]. NCBIGene:7157 is tumor protein p53 [4].

## Disease record identity

The disease record is named Li-Fraumeni syndrome [2]. The MedGen concept is titled Li-Fraumeni syndrome [6]. The literature index normalizes the entity as Li-Fraumeni Syndrome [7].

## TP53 as causal gene

Germline TP53 mutation is described as the cause of the syndrome, with dominant inheritance [19: "caused by a germline mutation of the TP53 gene on chromosome 17p13.1. It has an autosomal dominant pattern of inheritance with high penetrance"]. A case report likewise attributes the condition to germline TP53 mutations [21: "This hereditary condition is caused by germinal mutations in the TP53 gene"]. That report identified a TP53 variant on exon 5 in a Colombian patient [21: "on exon 5 of the TP53 gene, a deleterious mutation described previously in tumoural tissues"]. Phenotypic variability may reflect modifiers beyond the primary variant [22: "polymorphic variants in TP53 gene or in TP53-related genes, copy number variations in particular regions"].

## Supporting literature

One review is titled Li-Fraumeni Syndrome. [5]. Another is titled Li-Fraumeni syndrome. [10]. A further record is titled Li-Fraumeni Syndrome. [13]. A review is titled Li-Fraumeni syndrome heterogeneity. [16]. Linked publications include PMID 27617148 [9]. Another is PMID 27622479 [12]. Another is PMID 30333936 [15]. Another is PMID 31691207 [18].

Li-Fraumeni syndrome (LFS) is a cancer predisposition syndrome caused by a germline mutation of the TP53 gene on chromosome 17p13.1. It has an autosomal dominant pattern of inheritance with high penetrance. These patients have a very high lifetime cumulative risk of developing multiple malignancies
